STRUCTURE: GUPTA ARRESTS 2022

VO: From a coal mine to a dairy farm to a television station. Eskom. Transnet. Denel. SAA. SARS. The Gupta Family managed to worm their way in, allegedly corrupting the country’s institutions, politicians and even a president.

LINK: // Here we are, a possible 49 billion rand looted, our young democracy tested, our economy crippled. The so-called kingpins of state capture are finally in handcuffs.

VO: It’s been years since the Guptas’ influence and plundering was first exposed.

There’s been local and international economic sanctions, more than 520 million rands worth of assets seized. PAUSE.

They’ve been accused of treason, racketeering, extortion, money laundering and fraud - and yet the Gupta evaded justice. PAUSE.

Earlier this year, Justice Minister Ronald Lamola boldly told us, the government was ready to recover money anywhere in the world.

UPSOUND - JUSTICE THE COUNTDOWN
MINISTER: I believe that extradition will happen at some point.

VO: We were hopeful, but not convinced - perhaps we should have been.

UPSOUND - SABC / 702 / ALJAZEERA

VO: The news made global headlines on Monday - the alleged masterminds behind state capture have been caught.

The United Arab Emirates Ministry of Justice confirmed it acted on an international Red Notice request issued by Interpol in March.

UPSOUND GATE CLOSING

VO: The arrests at the Guptas’ luxury Dubai home in upmarket Emirates Hill, comes a year after South Africa signed an extradition treaty with the UAE.

JJ: You work behind the scenes// to protect the integrity of the process

VO: Advocate JJ du Toit is a legal expert in extradition.

MAC: WHy did it take so long? M6
JJ: You have to have your ducks in a row when you deal with extradition. You can't extradite while you busy with your investigation.

VO: This development is not a victory just yet.

KAREN: The arrest of the Guptas is just one small step in a path that is very long and filled with potential dangers for the National Prosecuting Authority.

VO: Karen Maughn is an Investigative legal journalist, having covered the Gupta’s state capture carnage for close to decade.

KAREN: The Guptas in many respects were leprosy on a body riddled with cancer. // a kind of absolutely unbelievable scenario in which a parallel, parallel administration effectively was operating, taking on the role of government and essentially operating solely to benefit itself. ANd that was what the Gupta enterprise was all about.

VO: The Zondo Commission into State Capture exposed the billions of Rands pilfered from taxpayers and outed the culprits for all to see.

Aubrey Matshiqi is a veteran political analyst.

AUBREY: //if there is any veracity in the claims and the allegations that have been made against the Gupta brothers this is taking us closer to the moment when the NPA will be able to prosecute them // The Guptas are not going to take this lying down.

LINK: The Guptas are no ordinary criminals. They are fugitives from justice who thought they'd gotten away with it when they vanished into thin air in 2018. But running away doesn't guarantee freedom.

VO: Atul and Rajesh Gupta were arrested on charges related to the alleged R25 million, Nulane Investment fraud, and money laundering case in Bloemfontein. While it’s a mere fraction of the looted state capture billions - this case is seemingly connected to other graft cases.

KAREN: it is apparent that the NPA in pursuing it, believes that this is a case where they can get a slam dunk conviction // and they are hoping that they'll be able to get motivated for a 15 to 30 year sentence for money laundering for the Guptas in this matter

VO: But that’s still a long way off.

JJ: //There will be lawyers in the Arabic system in Dubai that will be responsible //to put South Africa's case before their courts. Because remember, now, the extradition application will also have to be translated into the Arabic language..

VO: The heat is now on for the National Prosecuting Authority and the South African Police to navigate complex extradition procedures and the UAE legal system.

JJ: // You've got now 60 days to file your formal application where you set out in detail, you know, the charges and the grounds that you want to prosecute.

VO: Provided all the charges are disclosed before the extradition process is finalised, the charges don’t have to be limited to only the Nulane case.

JJ: Remember, a lot of water have run into the sea since then. The NPA will also consider at this moment to add additional counts // you have to tell the other country exactly the grounds on which you want the person to be extradited, and only on that counts. He can be tried in South Africa.

VO: Celebrating the arrests could be premature considering the United Arab Emirates’ track record.

HENNIE: It is a hub for global money laundering. // it's a tax haven. It thrives on secrecy.

VO: Hennie van Vuuren is from Open Secrets, a social justice non-profit organization.

HENNIE:I think we'd be naive to believe that the UAE has an interest //seeing justice for the crimes of state capture in South Africa. Those towering high rises in the desert were built largely not only off oil, but off dirty money that's been accumulated from many countries across the world and including the state capture loot from South Africa.

LINK: As a country, we've been through a lot. And with the Guptas it's been stop, start, stop, start. And even though this may feel like a step in the right direction, they have lots of money, have lots of influence, and are very well connected. So they're not going to go down without a fight.

VO: In Advocate Du Toit’s experience, it could take up to three years before the Guptas are back on South African soil.

JJ: the first thing that they want to do is to attack the process of why they were arrested on this red notice. And secondly, they want to also look at placing evidence before the court so that they can be released on bail

VO: While the Guptas remain in custody at an undisclosed police station since, there is no guarantee that an extradition will happen swiftly or smoothly. It’s likely that the Guptas would look to challenge the actual criminal charges.

KAREN: part of the extradition treaty that exists between South Africa and the UAE says that extradition must be refused in circumstances where a case is political or of a political nature.

VO: Unsurprisingly, the Guptas have maintained their innocence, denying all the allegations levelled against them and lawyered up with an extremely well-resourced legal team.

The Guptas have twice before successfully evaded prosecution.

KAREN: This is a high stakes game for the NPA. They simply cannot afford to mess this up.M11

MAC: Can we safely say that the days of interference are over?
AUBREY: No. The period of interfering with the NPA, in my view, is not over. // State capture occurred during a period we refer to as the 9 wasted year during Zuma’s Presidency. When in reality, state capture occurred before. And we're in the middle of state capture even now. M5

HENNIE:Ultimately what was at play during state capture was a system. // you know, you can take one or two players out of the system, but until you recognize that, // there's a bigger network of people at play, I don't think that we are able to talk conclusively about being in a post state capture phase.

VO: And the days of political intrigue and deception are also far from over.

In the space of a week, President Cyril Ramaphosa dominated news cycles when a political storm emerged around an alleged $4 million robbery at his Limpopo Farm, then the Guptas were arrested, and finally Public Protector Busisiwe Mkwebane was suspended.

This is leaked CCTV footage of the incident
PAUSE - LET IT PLAY FOR 1 SECOND ….

You can see the suspects lurking outside, before breaking into the house…
PAUSE - LET IT PLAY FOR 2 SECONDS

It’s a crime that took place two years ago but made it into national headlines courtesy of Former spy boss Arthur Fraser. He laid a complaint against the President for not reporting the crime.

AUBREY:But the timing is interesting, coinciding so interestingly with allegations that are being made against President Cyril Ramaphosa. So there are two possibilities here. It's a mere coincidence or it isn't. And if it isn't, the timing of the arrest of the Guptas may be part of a deception and counter deception strategy.

VO: Whatever the motivation behind these arrests, South Africans need accountability - now more than ever.

HENNIE: This is simply taking too long. If I steal a loaf of bread and, you know, which is far less complex than trying to steal a country. But I do know that the cops are going to come down hard on me // but we don't see that kind of accountability taking place for the very wealthy and the very powerful.

KAREN: The amazing thing with South AFricans is that we remain ever hopeful In the face of a lot of disappointment. // despite the obvious trepidation, a lot of people will hope that this is the time that we turn the corner.

VO: The Gupta arrests are a victory South Africans want to hold onto - even though a short lived celebration.


END








 
PROMOS
PROMO 1 - 21 SECONDS
VO: This week, two of the infamous Gupta brothers found themselves behind bars in Dubai.

Extradition is on the cards - but how long before they land in the dock in SOuth Africa if at all?

KAREN: The arrest of the Guptas is just one small step in a path that is very long and filled with potential dangers for the National Prosecuting Authority.


PROMO 2 - 21 SECONDS
VO: Billions of rands looted. An infamous family on the run evading justice. But this week their luck ran out - they were tracked down and arrested in Dubai.

A move that feels long overdue.

JJ: You have to have your ducks in a row when you deal with extradition. You can't extradite while you busy with your investigation.


PROMO 3 - 11 SECONDs
VO: Billions of rands looted. Our young democracy tested. Our economy crippled & state institutions hollowed out. The So-called kingpins of state capture are finally in handcuffs.
